problem: Zero-shot ObjectNav methods either score whole egocentric frames with VLMs (image-holistic, sparse value maps) or compare object labels directly in latent space, which is a weak proxy for spatial co-occurrence (similar-looking or similar-sounding categories need not share a room).
motivation: Efficient search needs semantic priors about which detected objects are near the target. Room types are a natural abstraction of functional co-occurrence, so mediating object relations through rooms could give a training-free, interpretable, open-vocabulary prior that respects the geometry of navigable space.
key_idea: Map each object label to a CLIP-derived Room Probability Vector over a small room lexicon, use the dot product of RPVs as object-target co-occurrence, and propagate it geodesically (FMM) into a value map to score frontiers.
insight: The RPV dot product ranks true co-occurrence anchors best (Top-5 Spearman 0.319, Recall@5 0.524, NDCG@5 0.715) because its multiplicative overlap suppresses high-entropy generic objects, though its full-row correlation is only modest (0.329). Geodesic FMM propagation beats isotropic Gaussian stamping only slightly (SR +0.005, SPL +0.003), which shows the gains are small and that Gaussians have compensating benefits, such as reacting immediately to detections in unknown space.
method: Perception pipeline: Mask2Former (ADE20K) blurs stuff classes plus door/window/curtain; YOLOE with the 1203 LVIS categories proposes detections (conf>0.5); SAM 3 cross-verifies the labels and gives masks, whose centroids are projected to world coordinates with depth; the target is always included in the prompts.

Room lexicon and RPV: 9 HM3D-style room types (bathroom, bedroom, dining room, garage, kitchen, hallway, laundry, living room, home office); CLIP text cosine similarity between the raw object label and each room label, then a softmax with tau=0.03, with no prompt templates.
Co-occurrence score: A_o = p_{o_d} · p_{o_t}, the dot product of the detected-object and target RPVs, interpreted as the joint probability that both share a room type.

Geodesic value map: each object emits A_o*exp(-d_geo^2/(2 sigma_o^2)) via Fast Marching Method flood-fill over the evolving occupancy grid, so signals do not pass through walls; cells are aggregated by mean over the objects reaching them.
Adaptive sigma: w=sqrt(A_o) expands the compressed [0.1,0.3] score range; sigma_o interpolates linearly from 1 m to 5 m with w, so relevant objects have a wide influence.

Frontier selection: frontiers are clustered within 0.5 m and each is scored by the median map value of its cells; the argmax is sent as a waypoint to a pretrained PointNav controller (VLFM-style). Perception runs every 3 steps.
Modes: initialize (12 turns for a 360° view), explore, and navigate once the target is detected.

setting.backbone: CLIP text encoder, YOLOE, SAM 3, Mask2Former (ADE20K, R50); pretrained PointNav controller (all frozen, no navigation training)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: forward 0.25 m, turn left/right 30°, stop (frontier waypoints executed by a PointNav policy)

numbers.backbone: CLIP text + YOLOE + SAM 3 + Mask2Former, FMM geodesic propagation
numbers.extra: Training-free; single-floor only (cannot solve 14.6% of multi-floor val episodes); success radius 1 m, 500 steps; 2000 episodes, 20 scenes
numbers.evidence: Table 1 HM3D ObjectNav Performance: RPV-V2 (ours) No 0.539 0.307 4.06

numbers.backbone: CLIP text + YOLOE + SAM 3 + Mask2Former, isotropic Gaussian propagation
numbers.extra: Ablation variant with Euclidean Gaussian stamping instead of FMM

numbers_note: Table 1 prints SR and SPL as fractions (0.539); converted to percentages. Split is the HM3D val split (labelled 'val' here). The VLFM baseline was re-evaluated locally by the authors.
results: RPV-V2 reaches SR 0.539 / SPL 0.307 / DTG 4.06 on HM3D val, a relative +3% SR and +1.3% SPL over the locally re-evaluated VLFM (0.523 / 0.303), and beats UIAP-OGN (0.523 / 0.290) and zero-shot L3MVN (0.504 / 0.231). PIRLNav has higher SR (0.641) but lower SPL (0.271), and RPV-V2 also exceeds trained L3MVN in SPL (0.255). Average inference time is 335.5 ms per step.
limitations: Gains over VLFM are small, and the FMM vs Gaussian ablation shows only +0.005 SR / +0.003 SPL; no significance testing is reported.
Built on a 2D VLFM map, so single-floor only, and it cannot solve 14.6% of HM3D val episodes that need multi-floor navigation.

RPV co-occurrence correlates only modestly with ground truth (Spearman about 0.32-0.33), high-entropy objects dilute the signal, and the policy has no information-gain exploration, so it over-commits to weak signals in sparse regions such as hallways.
